title: APGAR Score
sources: Critical Vector — Neonatology Pocket Guide: Assessment & APGAR
Apgar V. 1953; AAP–ACOG Committee Opinion on the Apgar Score (2015, reaffirmed)

changelog.change: Initial entry — the 5-sign score with an embedded additive calculator.

purpose: A rapid delivery-room description of the newborn's condition at 1 and 5 minutes (and every 5 min thereafter if the 5-min score is < 7). It describes the response to resuscitation — it does NOT direct it, and a single value is neither sensitive nor specific for outcome in an individual infant.

body.text: Resuscitation is driven by heart rate, respiratory effort, and tone — start it (see NRP) without waiting for the 1-minute Apgar. A 5-minute Apgar ≤ 5 is associated with higher risk of an adverse outcome at a population level, but is not diagnostic for an individual and does not by itself establish a hypoxic-ischaemic cause.

interpretation.label: 0–3 — low; initiate / continue resuscitation per NRP
4–6 — moderately abnormal; may need stimulation, oxygen, or PPV
≥ 7 — reassuring; routine care with ongoing evaluation

buildNote: Tier 1. Descriptive, not directive. Related: nrp-algorithm, neonatal-hie-cooling.
